title.value: IMPROVING SOURCE SEPARATION BY EXPLICITLY MODELING DEPENDENCIES BETWEEN SOURCES
title.justification: The title accurately captures the focus of the paper, which is about using a new method to improve source separation by modeling dependencies between sound sources in a mixture.
title.quote:
IMPROVING SOURCE SEPARATION BY EXPLICITLY MODELING DEPENDENCIES BETWEEN SOURCES

Ethan Manilow ^{1,2,∗} , Curtis Hawthorne ^{1} , Cheng-Zhi Anna Huang ^{1} , Bryan Pardo ^{2} , Jesse Engel ^{1}

extractions.description: This paper discusses a novel method for improving source separation in audio by explicitly modeling the dependencies between different sources. It introduces an Orderless Neural Autoregressive Density Estimator (NADE) approach with a block Gibbs sampling procedure that enhances separation performance by leveraging interdependencies between sources. The method is validated using two datasets and shows improved results compared to traditional methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on music and audio source separation methods and does not address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes. No sustainability-related applications or impacts are highlighted.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our work draws inspiration from COCONET [26], which is a generative model of musical scores and uses contextual note information to infill new musical voices. We expand the scope of their Orderless NADE [1, 2] formulation to the continuous domain of audio signals, by modeling sources in a source separation context.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any of the listed Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories, as its focus is on audio processing techniques rather than sustainability.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we propose alterations to the training and inference procedures of existing neural networks to account for contextual information between different sources in a musical scene.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not touch upon secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes; it's centered on enhancing audio processing through machine learning without links to ecological or climate issues.
secondary_categories.quote: We conduct a set of experiments to validate the proposed training and testing setup. In our experiments, we test the effect of training a separation network using our Orderless NADE and block Gibbs sampling procedures.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no direct connection to any Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories as the paper specifically details audio processing techniques.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a new method for training a supervised source separation system that aims to learn the interdependent relationships between all combinations of sources in a mixture.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The absence of any relevance to specific sustainable development sub-categories reinforces the non-affiliation of this paper with ecological or climate considerations.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We train one network for each of the two datasets that we test: MUSDB18 [31] and Slakh2100 [32].

applications.justification: The paper offers a novel approach to music source separation by explicitly modeling dependencies, which enhances audio processing capabilities.
applications.quote: By pairing this training method with a block Gibbs sampling procedure at inference time, we demonstrate that the network can iteratively improve its separation performance by conditioning a source estimate on its earlier source estimates.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's focus lies entirely outside the realm of climate or ecology, therefore requiring no new category related to sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: Experiments on two source separation datasets show that training a Demucs model with an Orderless NADE approach and using Gibbs sampling (up to 512 steps) at inference time strongly outperforms a Demucs baseline that uses a standard regression loss and direct (one step) estimation of sources.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper's principal subject is music source separation through novel machine learning methods, it doesn't necessitate a new sustainable development sub-category.
